samples.marker: XWiki exploit: sends Groovy RCE with a reverse-shell payload
execution: Module-level URL-encodes media=rss and a macro-breakout payload as text.
Appends the query to the operator-supplied base URL plus /bin/get/Main/SolrSearch, performs urlopen and reads its response.
The Groovy expression invokes a string command through execute() and prints the process stdout. Its embedded Bash command attempts to redirect interactive shell I/O to an external TCP endpoint.
samples.judgement: An active request carrying command injection and a concrete reverse-shell payload tips the balance to malicious; no authorized assessment context accompanies it.
limits: No live exploit request was sent. Target XWiki version and reachability are unknown.

Groovy String.execute uses Runtime.exec(String), without an intervening shell parser. The payload omits bash -c, so its redirection tokens are arguments rather than working shell redirections. Successful reverse-shell establishment is not claimed.
changes: Preserved all three hostile reverse-shell rules and the suspicious shell-pattern rule.
Corrected the Python reverse-shell description to describe an embedded command rather than a local socket opening.
Added generalizable Groovy macro-breakout and HTTP-client co-occurrence detections, with no sample IP, port, or filename gate.

samples.marker: Runner dumper: targets CI worker memory and writes it to stdout
execution: Lists numeric /proc entries and returns the first PID whose cmdline contains the bytes Runner.Worker.
Opens that PID maps and unbuffered binary mem files. Parses hexadecimal region bounds, selects readable regions, skips addresses above sys.maxsize, seeks, and reads each region.
Writes raw read bytes to sys.stdout.buffer; OSError skips the failed region. The script does not itself filter secrets, encode output, make network requests, or elevate privileges.
samples.judgement: Automatic selection of the credential-bearing CI worker and bulk memory output differs from the upstream user-selected diagnostic. Published incident research independently documents this runner-targeted routine in the tj-actions compromise. Those facts tip the balance to likely malicious; no deployment or authorization is invented.
limits: Needs permission to read the selected process memory. Neither privileges nor deployment are supplied.
The original referenced gist now returns 404. The local positive fixture and published source/incident descriptions support identification; a recovered-original-gist hash match is not asserted.

Both retained hostile rules describe aspects of one credential-dumping operation. There is no evidence to invent separate exfiltration, persistence, elevation, or supply-chain execution behavior in this standalone file.
changes: Moved the three firing credential-memory composites from legacy dump/process to credential-access/memory and updated their exact references.
Retained both hostile patterns, now requiring a bound proc-memory path/open/read/write chain and actual seek/read-to-write operations.
Renamed path-only dumper to memory-path-cluster and corrected three path-only suspicious rules to notable references; no underlying path matches were erased.
Promoted the sensitive maps/memory helper from baseline to notable.
Added generic stream seeking, read-result-to-write, and bound proc-memory-read observations.

samples.marker: Electron session helper: caller supplies tokens; fix theft overclaims
execution: Exports openSession; importing the module alone only loads Electron and exports the function.
Uses a caller-selected session partition and visible BrowserWindow. Registers a header hook restricted to admin.microsoft.com and writes a Bearer header from the supplied access token.
Posts that access token to the official OWA auth.owa endpoint as an encoded bearer form. Any Set-Cookie response removes the header hook, even outside the filtered admin site.

A hidden window in the same partition posts the supplied refresh token to the official Entra OAuth endpoint, checks for an ESTSAUTH cookie, then posts a changed admin-resource scope. Token JSON is never parsed or otherwise consumed.

If no ESTSAUTH cookie exists the function throws before the second refresh/navigation and does not close the hidden window. Otherwise it closes the hidden window, navigates the visible window to caller-supplied serviceUrl, and returns it.
samples.judgement: The supported behavior is using credentials supplied by the caller for authentication at the issuer/service. This excerpt has no acquisition, third-party export, user impersonation claim, or deceptive installation path. Names such as captured are not evidence of theft. Authorized SSO/session bootstrapping explains the same effects, so the balance favors benign dual-use code. Suspicious session replay remains accurately detected.
limits: The caller, credential ownership, consent, and surrounding product are unavailable; malicious use of stolen tokens remains possible.
The code does not prove that refresh grants mint browser cookies or bypass MFA. Existing session cookies and successful server responses are not guaranteed.
changes: Renamed stolen-token-to-owa-session to owa-bearer-session-replay, retained its matcher, and set suspicious; removed the unsupported mailbox-collection ATT&CK mapping.

Moved generic request-hook/Authorization-assignment/Microsoft-client-ID co-occurrence to notable HTTP authorization-header mechanics with an accurate name and description. Same matcher and exclusion remain.
Preserved hidden-browser-refresh-to-session-cookie as suspicious and preserved every accurate protocol/window/hook finding.

verification.facts: cleave facts run on each original; no hidden encoding or obfuscation was found; URL/form serialization is transport encoding
verification.dependency_review: No firing trait in this batch was attributed to a fetched dependency. The Electron module is an import; no dependent-package exception was introduced.
verification.archive_review: The three submitted artifacts are plain source files. The existing xz-compressed memory-dumper positive was decompressed and retested separately.

shared_rule_audit.finding: Exact and ancestor YAML references inspected before editing. Only the two intended memory-path consumers required renamed IDs; no directory-selector expansion was introduced. The moved memory-secret-context atom references its secret markers by full legacy IDs. Session-replay composites have no YAML consumers.

detection_losses_and_disagreements: No supported reverse-shell or actual runner-memory-dump coverage was lost in the focused controls.
Path-only catalogs no longer receive hostile dump findings; sensitive path observations remain notable.

Two unsupported hostile OAuth labels become one suspicious replay signal and one notable header-rewrite observation; hidden refresh remains suspicious. The existing OWA positive retains its replay finding at suspicious because it supplies no evidence of stolen credentials.

At current default calibration, XWiki is ML-hostile before and after. Electron is ML-benign before and after, despite the old hostile rule labels. The runner dumper is ML-benign at the default threshold before and after; it previously appeared only at looser L5000 and is off the calibrated grid after accurate corrections. This is a classifier miss, with both hostile memory rules still firing.

The engine reports source-local flow limitations; all relevant paths were independently traced, including mocked I/O tests. The installed model feature specification is v18 while the extractor advertises v19; model results are reported as observed.
